findings.evidence: Ultrasound scan left breast showing cystic duct changes suggestive of mammary duct ectasia.

panels.rationale: Single ultrasound panel of the left breast with caption and in-text description explicitly identifying cystic ductal changes consistent with mammary duct ectasia; it is a real patient image showing the target disease manifestation.
panels.attribution_text: Al Blooshi et al. Bloody nipple discharge in young children: mammary duct ectasia as a benign, self-limiting condition.. Journal of surgical case reports 2026. doi:10.1093/jscr/rjag028. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasound scan left breast showing cystic duct changes suggestive of mammary duct ectasia.
in_text_mentions: Targeted ultrasonography of the left breast was subsequently performed as the primary imaging modality. Sonographic evaluation demonstrated a small hypoechoic retroareolar lesion measuring ~10 by 2 millimeters with internal cystic ductal changes and absence of internal vascularity on color Doppler assessment. These findings were consistent with mammary duct ectasia and are illustrated in Fig. 1.

panels.rationale: H&E section shows irregularly dilated ducts with inspissated eosinophilic secretions, dense periductal lymphoplasmacytic inflammation and concentric fibrosis, diagnostic of mammary duct ectasia in a real patient biopsy.
panels.attribution_text: Ijaz et al. Mammary Duct Ectasia Presenting As MRI Non-mass Enhancement in a RAD51C Carrier With Pituitary Adenoma.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.106937. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: H&E-stained section, magnification 10x. Irregularly dilated ducts containing inspissated eosinophilic secretions, dense periductal lymphoplasmacytic inflammation, and concentric fibrosis (indicated by arrows).
in_text_mentions: MRI-guided core biopsy was performed from the central left breast. Pathology examination shows multiple irregularly dilated large ducts containing inspissated eosinophilic secretions (Figure 4). Dense periductal lymphoplasmacytic inflammation with concentric fibrosis was noted. Coarse dystrophic microcalcifications were present, predominantly within duct walls (Figure 5). No epithelial atypia, necrosis, or carcinoma was identified; the myoepithelial layer was intact. Immunohistochemistry was not performed; routine H&E was sufficient for definitive diagnosis.
panels.copyright: Ijaz et al. Mammary Duct Ectasia Presenting As MRI Non-mass Enhancement in a RAD51C Carrier With Pituitary Adenoma.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.106937. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.

panels.rationale: Single axial T1 pre-contrast breast MRI of a real patient showing T1-hyperintense ductal ectasia in the central left breast, arrow-indicated, in an article specifically about mammary duct ectasia. No skin visible, so skin tone null; no age or ethnicity stated.
panels.attribution_text: Ijaz et al. Mammary Duct Ectasia Presenting As MRI Non-mass Enhancement in a RAD51C Carrier With Pituitary Adenoma.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.106937. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Breast MRI axial T1 pre-contrast: T1-hyperintense ductal ectasia in the central left breast (indicated by arrow).
in_text_mentions: Axial T1-weighted pre-contrast images demonstrated T1-hyperintense ductal ectasia (Figure 2), and dynamic post-contrast images showed segmental non-mass enhancement with plateau kinetics in the central left breast (Figure 3). “Non-mass enhancement” on breast MRI refers to areas of abnormal contrast uptake that do not form a discrete mass but instead appear as diffuse or regional enhancement, which can be difficult to distinguish from malignant processes. Differential considerations included fibrocystic change, pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia, ductal carcinoma in situ, and invasive carcin

panels.rationale: Grayscale breast ultrasound of the patient shows a small smoothly marginated complex (retention-type) cystic lesion marked by a red arrow; the article title and in-text course (recurrent inflamed cyst, granulation tissue on FNA) attribute this lesion to mammary duct ectasia, matching the galactocele-like/retention cyst finding. The image is a real patient study with no third-party copyright noted.
panels.attribution_text: Ijaz et al. Mammary Duct Ectasia Presenting As MRI Non-mass Enhancement in a RAD51C Carrier With Pituitary Adenoma.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.106937. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Targeted breast ultrasound showed a 6 × 4 millimeter smoothly marginated complex cystic lesion in the right breast at the 11 o'clock position (indicated by arrow).
in_text_mentions: At age 46, the patient presented with a two-month history of a right breast lump prompting further diagnostic evaluation. Ultrasound demonstrated a 6 × 4 mm smoothly marginated complex cystic lesion at the 11 o'clock position, Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RAD) category 4 (Figure 1). Fine-needle aspiration showed acute inflammation and granulation tissue without malignancy. She experienced recurrent cyst inflammation requiring aspiration and antibiotics, with negative cultures.
